ops.title: prepare_graph is already flat in transcript size; long-session stalls are concurrent-dispatch bursts
ops.body:
Order (meta-desk-3, Nov 6): make prepare_graph incremental, because each dispatch's prepare_graph re-reads the 400 MB transcript in 697-741 ms. Measured before building; the premise does not hold.

Harness: /Users/yasyf/.vcache/scratch/snapshot-oversize-clip/measure/measure.py, run with the installed capt-hook 12.121.37 env (cc-transcript 14.46.16, its cc-transcript-owner through captain_hook.testing.snapshots.FixtureOwner, default config). Each round: load_transcript (acquire), then prepare_graph exactly as PreparedGraphEvidence.require sends it (thread_ids [], roots [], direct_paths [], graph_limits()), then append one user line. Copies of session 72c2336c under the measure dir.

| Root transcript | Sidechains | acquire, first / later | prepare_graph | source bytes read | discovery entries |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.1 MB (prefix) | none | 188 ms / 8-9 ms | 3 ms | 0 | 0 |
| 401.6 MB | none | 159 ms / 9 ms | 4-6 ms | 0 | 0 |
| 401.6 MB | 356 jsonl (1.34 GB, 712 entries) | 163 ms / 9-10 ms | 22-24 ms | 0 | 712 |

prepare_graph reads no transcript bytes at either size, and its time does not grow with the root: 3 ms at 1 MB against 4-6 ms at 400 MB, the same appended tail each round. What it scales with is the sidechain directory: 712 entries examined on every call, 23 ms.

Production timing for the same session (daemon logs, dispatches whose root is dar-meta-desk-3): 26,210 dispatches, 1,739 over 700 ms. The three stalls fall in bursts of concurrent dispatches for this one session. 12:35:11.622: a PostToolUse at 1,159 ms ran alongside PreToolUse 2462 (287 ms) and 2463 (118 ms). 12:55:12-13: PostToolUse at 1,656 ms and 1,043 ms (queue_ms 10.8), PreToolUse 3089 at 3,274 ms (queue_ms 12.1), PostToolUse at 834 ms. 14:04:04-06: PostToolUse at 997 ms, SubagentStart at 493 ms, PreToolUse 299 at 1,021 ms. Single dispatches between bursts take 20-200 ms.

Reading: the 0.75 s goes to waiting behind concurrent work for the same session (or the shared owner and worker on a Mac at load 12-14), not to graph preparation proportional to transcript size. An incremental graph would not change these numbers. Untested next step: replay one burst (several concurrent PreToolUse/PostToolUse dispatches against one root through the real capt-hookd host) with per-request queue and work timings from the owner, to name the lock or queue they wait on.
